title: Siegard capability declarations
description: Contract for src/claude/capabilities.declaration.json, the authored set the generator turns into the distribution manifest's catalog. foundation/0007 R21 makes a declaration a separate artifact referencing schemas/skill.json and schemas/agent.json rather than extending them, and R23 keeps it out of the distribution. One file rather than one per capability, on the precedent src/claude/hooks/hooks.declaration.json sets: an authored declaration stays behind and the generator ships what it computes. A .json beside a component would also break the closed directory set of foundation/0008 R7, which admits only agents/*.md under agents/.

declarations.description: One entry per capability that carries a declaration. That every capability carries one is foundation/0007 R1; how many exist here is what its Outstanding evidence condition 1 still owes.

identifier.description: The capability's stable identifier (R3), equal to the component's own name. It carries no prefix: foundation/0008 R20 makes the plugin name the namespace, and a reserved prefix would be a second one.

class.description: The capability class from the closed set foundation/0006 R1 holds. It decides which parts below are required of this declaration.

objective.description: What the capability is for and when to choose it, deciding case first (R4). It does not describe how the capability works: a consumer choosing between two needs to tell them apart.

inputs.description: Every input named, each either required or carrying a stated default (R5). An empty array declares that the capability takes none.

outputs.description: What it returns, and under which contract version. Empty where the capability returns nothing another capability consumes: R7 requires a contract version for an output a consumer branches on, and a procedure whose only product is a report for a person has none. Forcing an entry here would put a schema around prose, and a second declared producer behind an artifact one capability authors.

consumed_artifacts.description: What it reads that it was not given (R8), so a reader can tell what it depends on without executing it.

produced_artifacts.description: Artifact classes it writes. Required of every class that writes; absent means it writes none.

required_context.description: What knowledge it needs in scope, in ontology terms rather than file paths (R9). Naming all six node types declares the whole ontology and narrows nothing, which R9's own contingency already anticipates.

deterministic_behavior.description: What it decides the same way every time (R10). Every entry here is decided by a script or a hook (R11); a property listed while a prompt decides it is a defect in the declaration.

judgment.description: What it decides by reasoning, and therefore what may vary (R10). An empty array is a claim that nothing varies, which R10 permits only where no model produces the output.

assertions.description: Which assertions bind its output, and where none does (R12). An assertion binds one knowledge object — a schema check is not one and belongs to the output's contract version instead.

grant.description: The tools and permissions its declared steps require, and nothing wider (R14). Required of every class that executes; the absence of a statement is not a grant.

failure_outcomes.description: How it reports being unable to proceed (R15). Each is a named closed value a consumer branches on, with a reason a caller can act on.

deprecation.description: Present only while this capability is going away. Its presence is one of the two checkable facts a status is derived from — the other being whether the distribution installs it — so `deprecated` is computed rather than written down, which R17 requires. Absent means active.

replacement.description: The capability that takes this one's work, or the words that state plainly that none does. R15 admits both and admits no silence: a consumer told a capability is going away and not told what replaces it has been given half a migration.

reason.description: Why it is going away, in terms a consumer can act on rather than a changelog line.

default.description: The stated default R5 demands of a non-required input. A value supplied silently when the field is absent is the hidden default foundation/0005 R16b rejects.

contract.description: The contract version a consumer selects behavior on (R7), never inferred from shape.

bound.description: False names the gap R12 requires rather than leaving absence to read as coverage.

knowledge_object.description: The knowledge object the assertion binds. Required where bound is true, because an assertion with no knowledge object is not one.
